name: rail-upfront-no-recourse
represents: The rail's upfront flow: settle first, then execute the service, then respond. Same absence of recourse as B0a, different ordering.
profile_v1_violations: no verifier registry violates minVerifiers >= 3 * maxAssignments + 5
cannot_express: no way to distinguish 'the seller never started' from 'the seller started and failed', because settlement precedes execution and nothing records execution
no deadline on the response, so a silent seller is not in violation of anything
harness_special_cases: this arm is the only one where the non-delivery window opens before any service work exists; the controller must be able to kill the seller process between settle and execute and record that the payment is already final
the D-sweep does not apply; emit one point at D = 0
scenario F4 (settled, no response) is the discriminating run against B0a: here it is reachable with zero seller effort

cheater_scenarios.steady_cheat: Same as B0a, plus a strictly cheaper attack: the seller collects without executing. Cheater gain per purchase rises from g to v because the service cost is not incurred.
cheater_scenarios.S5_burst: Same as B0a. The cheapest burst attack in the whole comparison, since the attacker's marginal cost per settlement is near zero.

expected_outcome.honest_seller_cost: Zero, as B0a. The honest seller is strictly better off here than under any mechanism arm; that asymmetry is the point of the comparison.

operating_point_note: Values written "op:<expr>" are read from experiments/operating-point.json (see experiments/controller/operating_point.py); this file keeps no copy of g, v, p, L or the rates.
